Welcome
On behalf of the children, staff and governors, I would like to warmly welcome you to our school website. It is designed to give you a taste of our wonderful small rural primary school and the excellent things that happen here, and to provide important information to parents, and the wider community.
I am very proud to be the head teacher of our amazing school. It is a privilege to lead the staff and the excellent work they do in providing an environment which enables every child to learn, grow and succeed together in our school community. Most of all, it is a joy to work with the fabulous children we have at Burghclere; they achieve highly both academically and personally through the supportive and aspirational learning environment, pastoral care and the amazing extracurricular opportunities they have.
I hope that you enjoy your visit to our website and find the information you are looking for. If you have any further questions or, even better, would like to see our school in action and meet the staff and children, please contact the school office at adminoffice@burghclere.hants.sch.uk or by telephone on 01635 278523.
Thank you for visiting and we look forward to meeting you soon.

pageCache.pageTitle: Burghclere Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
At Burghclere Primary school, we aim to provide a happy, inclusive, nurturing environment where everyone is learning, growing and succeeding together, so that they have the skills, knowledge and values to make a positive difference to their communities in an ever-changing world.
At Burghclere we value:
Respect - we show respect for people and property by being thoughtful, patient, kind, inclusive and polite.
Determination - we show determination through setting aspirational personal goals, striving to be the best we can be, embracing mistakes, reflecting on our learning, and putting effort into all we do.
Collaboration - we show collaboration through valuing teamwork, supporting others, being attentive listeners, being able to compromise and sharing our ideas.
Responsibility - we show responsibility through understanding how our choices can impact others, and by developing behaviour that promotes trust and personal development.
Curiosity - we show curiosity through exploring, investigating, questioning and showing an interest in the world around us.
Vision and Values

British Values
Promoting British Values
The Education Act (2002) requires schools, as part of a broad and balanced curriculum, to promote the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of pupils at the school.
In 2011, the Government defined British Values as democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths and beliefs.
Burghclere Primary School promotes these values through our mission statement, our values, our curriculum and our enrichment activities.
UN CRC Article 12: Children have the right to say what they think should happen when adults are making decisions that affect them, and to have their opinions taken into account.
Links to school values: Inquisitiveness, Supportiveness, Creativity, Respect
Value – The Rule of Law
UN CRC Article 19: Governments should ensure that children are properly cared for and protect them from violence, abuse and neglect by their parents, or anyone else who looks after them.
Links to school values: Respect
Value – Individual Liberty
UN CRC Article 31: All children have a right to relax and play and to join in a wide range of activities.
UN CRC Article 15: Children have the right to meet together and to join groups and organisations as long as this does not stop other people from enjoying their rights.
Links to school values: Aspiration, Supportiveness, Reflection, Respect
Value – Mutual Respect
UN CRC Article 2: The Convention applies to everyone whatever their race, religion, abilities, whatever they think or say and whatever type of family they come from.
UN CRC Article 30: Children have a right to learn and use the language and customs of their families, whether these are shared by the majority of people in the country or not.
Links to school values: Respect, Supportiveness
Value – Tolerance of Different Faiths and Beliefs
UN CRC Article 14: Children have the right to think and believe what they want and to practise their religion, as long as they are not stopping other people from enjoying their rights. Parents should guide their children on these matters.
Links to school values: Respect, Inquisitiveness
British Values

Welcome
Welcome to Burghclere Primary School!
Burghclere Primary School is a small rural school in the village of Burghclere with a happy, inclusive, nurturing environment where everyone is learning, growing and succeeding together, so that they have the skills and values to make a positive difference to their communities in an ever-changing world.
We are surrounded by beautiful countryside and this is reflected in the outdoor learning spaces we have, which include a large playing field, playground, woodland adventure playground, garden and outdoor learning environment with a fire-pit, bug hotel and chickens. Our school building has a large hall, a cosy library, a space for our after-school club and four spacious classrooms for the following year groups: Year R, Year 1/2, Year 3/4 and Year 5/6. Each classroom has an interactive whiteboard and resources to support the teaching and learning appropriate to the age group. Our EYFS classroom has a large outdoor space which includes a sandpit, a nature kitchen, a stage and space for construction and water play- and so much more! We are very proud of our inclusive environment which is adapted to meet the needs of all our children.
We offer a rich broad curriculum which not only meets the requirements of the national curriculum, giving children the knowledge and skills they need to succeed in the next stage of their learning, but offers unique opportunities which give each child the chance to develop the values and confidence to become global citizens who want to make a positive difference to their communities. These extra opportunities in our curriculum include Muddy Monday outdoor learning afternoons, small group tuition to play a brass instrument, and, as part of our work with the JDO Foundation, collaboration projects with schools across the world through the use of technology - making our children true global citizens!
We also offer a wide range of other opportunities for our children. These include lunchtime and after-school clubs such as running, football, art, choir, nature ninjas and netball. We have a school council and Junior Road Safety Officers who lead initiatives and fund-raising activities across the school. Our Year 6 pupils all have a leadership role, such as play leaders, music maestros, librarians and house captains - who organise house competitions and take the lead in collaborative house projects. We have a brass band who play at the church, school celebrations and wider community events such as the Newbury spring festival at the Corn Exchange theatre. Our children perform at the O2 arena in London as part of the Young Voices choir. Our Y5/6 children enjoy a weeks long residential at a PGL centre - one of many visits and trips they have.
This website aims to give you a taste of our wonderful primary school, as well as providing important information for both parents and pupils.
I hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find the information you are looking for. If you have any further questions or, even better, would like to see our school in action, please contact the school office at adminoffice@burghclere.hants.sch.uk
Thank you for visiting!
Mrs Beulah Letchford Headteacher

School Opening Hours and Timetable
Times of School Sessions (32.5 hours)
8:45 a.m. School day begins/Registration
10:30 a.m. Breaktime (15 minutes)
12:00 noon. End of morning session
1:00 p.m. Registration
2:00 p.m. Afternoon break (15 minutes KS1 only)
2:50pm Collective Worship
3:10 p.m. End of School Day (KS1)
3:15 p.m. End of School Day (KS2)
The School Day begins at 8:45 a.m. with children arriving no earlier than 8:35 a.m on to the school playground. Classroom doors will open at 8:40 a.m.
Children in Year R may enter their classroom at 8:35 a.m. for a settling in period, accompanied by their parents, in the first few weeks.
In the event of a problem with collecting, or dropping off, your child, would you please inform the Office of any delay as soon as possible.
Children are released from the classroom door to the parent or designated adult, by the class teacher.
The school day starts at 8.45 a.m. and children should be in the classroom for that time. The late arrival of children to school causes unnecessary disruption to the classes and creates difficulties with regard to registration and dinner numbers etc. Please note that children arriving late will be given a “late mark” and parents will be informed if the frequency of “late marks” is too high. Persistent lateness can also now result in the issuing of a Penalty Notice fine.
Any children arriving after the school gate is locked must report via the front entrance to the Administration staff in the School Office before going to their class.
Late arrivals for medical appointments which cannot be rearranged are perfectly understandable. You should let the school know in advance if at all possible.

Good Vibes Music Academy
Good Vibes Music Academy provide individual and small group tuition for children who are keen to learn to play a musical instrument, or develop their singing skills. Children are learning to play a range of brass instruments, guitars and keyboards. The school receives a small amount of money for the lessons taken, which is then used to provide whole school musical workshops, and to pay for the band rehearsals.
If you would like to find out more please visit their website: https://www.goodvibesmusicacademy.co.uk/
Wider School Community
Good Vibes Music Academy

Governors' Award
The Governors’ Award
The Governors’ Award is open to all pupils at the school, in any class, and is awarded towards the end of the academic year to the pupil whose behaviour and values throughout the year have been exemplary and who best capture the values of our school. It is not awarded for academic excellence.
We make the process of identifying the winner as fair and objective as possible. In the summer term, the class teachers anonymously nominate three or four candidates with a paragraph that encapsulates why the pupil should be considered, giving specific examples to support their nominations.
The Governors of the school meet and carefully consider the nominations and vote for their preferred candidate. Staff Governors do not vote. The pupil with the majority vote is the winner.
It is very exciting for the Governors and children alike as we have no knowledge of who we choose until the process is complete!
The pupil selected is informed at the end of year Celebration assembly in front of all their peers and given the prestigious trophy and prize from the Chair of the Governors. Their picture then adorns the entrance hall for the following academic year.

pageCache.pageTitle: Burghclere Primary School - Prospective Parents: Why Choose us?
pageCache.text:
Prospective Parents: Why Choose us?
All schools work hard to do the best they can for their pupils- and we are no exception! Our pupils are happy, well-supported and cared for, achieve very well academically, and have values and skills which prepare them for the next stage in their educational journeys - so they can go on to make a positive difference to their communities and the wider world. So what else can our school offer your child that makes choosing us the best decision you will make?
Marshmallows around the firepit!
We have a beautiful outside learning area which our youngest children use every week in their Welly Wednesday sessions. These sessions are based on the Forest School approach, with children involved in a range of outdoor learning activities, including playing with the chickens, hunting for bugs, gardening, building shelters, creating works of art, exploring and enjoying the natural environment, and so much more - whatever the weather! The favourite activity is always cooking around the firepit- and toasting marshmallows is at the top of the list! Our older children have regular opportunities to learn in this environment too, including conducting science experiments, recording the weather and even performing their speeches from Macbeth around the cauldron!
We are passionate about music at Burghclere- it is a unique part of our school's history. All our children have the opportunity to learn to play a brass instrument when they are in Year 3- this is fully funded by our active Band committee, along with weekly band tuition for all our members. Our band performs in school, at the local church, with local brass bands and at venues in Newbury. We have strong links with Good Vibes Music Academy, who offer tuition in keyboard, guitar and vocals. Along with our school choir and strong music curriculum, music will continue to thrive into the future too!
Collaborative projects with schools across the globe!
All our Y5/6 children have their own Chromebooks, which they use to work on collaborative learning projects with children in other countries. We are part of the JDO Foundation, who support us by providing the technology and opportunity for our children to participate in this amazing scheme. Each term, the children have a 'hangout' with their learning partners and collaborate on learning projects which include writing and publishing stories, developing fitness programmes, creating their own Google Earth, and so much more! Computing, and the use of a range of technologies, apps and websites, is taught across the school- it is a core part of what we do. Our children leave with computing skills and confidence beyond their peers - setting them up for the future!
Sports and activities galore!
Providing rich experiences and opportunities outside the curriculum is a key feature of our school. This can be through dance and drama workshops; celebrating events like World Book Day, the King's coronation and the Olympics; singing at the O2 arena; running a mini-marathon; watching performances at the theatre; going on adventurous activity residentials and so many curriculum trips! We offer a wide variety of clubs, including choir, dance, computing, art, running, netball, football, rugby and athletics. We take part in a lot of sports events, and have been very successful. We recently won the small schools trophy for the Basingstoke and Deane indoor athletics, and won the rugby league trophy against local schools. ALL our children in Y2-Y6 have the opportunity to represent the school in at least one interschool sports event every year.
Our school has a popular Breakfast Club running from 8:00am each morning. It offers toast and fruit in a family-style breakfast around the table. Our After-School Club runs until 5:15pm and children have the chance to play games with their friends, inside and outside, do craft activities and relax after a busy day at school!
And there's so much more!
To find out more about what we can offer your child, take a read of our newsletters, or, even better, come and visit us and see our wonderful school in action!
Spaces Available for September 2026!
We currently have spaces available for our Year 1, Year 2, Year 3, Year 4 and Year 5 cohorts for September 2026. Please visit the school during the summer term and find out about all we can offer your child. We look forward to meeting you.
Please contact the school office if you have any queries!
Open Mornings - September 2027 intake! jpg
Prospective Parents: Why Choose us?

Curriculum
At Burghclere Primary school, we aim to provide a happy, inclusive and nurturing environment where everyone is learning, growing and succeeding together, so that they have the skills, knowledge and values to make a positive difference to their communities in an ever-changing world.
All aspects of our curriculum are accessible to all children, irrespective of their ethnic background, gender, disability, religious or linguistic background. We strive hard to meet the needs of those pupils with special educational needs, those with disabilities, those who are more able, those with special gifts or talents, and the children who are learning English as an additional language. We provide a rich, challenging curriculum which stretches all our children, developing their skills and knowledge in a carefully planned and progressive way. It builds on the foundations of the EYFS curriculum and enables pupils to meet the requirements of the National Curriculum and prepare them for the next stage of their education and beyond. Staff monitor and track children's progress to ensure their academic potential is continuously developed and they achieve highly.
Curriculum Implementation
The curriculum is all the planned activities that we organise in order to promote learning and personal growth and development. It includes not only the formal requirements of the National Curriculum, which are developed to meet the needs of our children and the aims of our curriculum, but also the range of extracurricular activities that the school organises in order to enrich the experience of the children. It also includes the ‘hidden curriculum’, or what the children learn from the way they are treated and expected to behave. Our school values of inquisitiveness, aspiration, supportiveness, creativity, resilience, independence, reflection and respect, are key drivers for ensuring children are ready to take their place in the world.
The EYFS curriculum meets the requirements of the EYFS statutory framework. There are seven curriculum goals identified by the school as areas for children to achieve to be ready for Year 1. There are termly topics which form the starting point for learning each term in the seven areas of learning and development. Learning outdoors is a key part of the curriculum and Monday afternoons are devoted to our forest school approach. Learning to read using phonics is a priority and the school uses the Little Wandle phonics scheme to teach children to read. Books are everywhere and reading for pleasure and purpose happens daily. Drawing Club encourages children to apply their writing skills and develop their vocabulary and is based around core texts. The Mastering Number programme teaches children to become fluent in numbers and other learning activities teach other aspects of the maths curriculum. Discovery Time is a core part of the EYFS curriculum - children are given the opportunity to develop their knowledge and skills through the learning environment. The curriculum is the foundation for the rest of the school curriculum, which builds upon the knowledge and skills children have learnt.
The curriculum is taught on a two-yearly cycle. It builds on the learning in EYFS and prepares children with the knowledge and skills they need for Key Stage 2 across all subject areas. Emphasis is placed on the development of early reading through the Little Wandle phonics scheme, as well as developing writing skills, taught through learning journeys around a text; and maths skills, which are taught following the Mastery Number programme and White Rose maths scheme, whilst ensuring children have experiences that are memorable and enjoyable through a broad range of subjects. Outdoor learning on Monday afternoons following a forest school approach is a highlight of the children's week and gives them opportunities to work with younger pupils and explore the natural world.
The curriculum is taught on a two-yearly cycle in Y3/4 and in Y5/6. It builds on the knowledge and skills acquired in Key Stage 1 and prepares them for the next stage of learning in secondary school. All subjects in the national curriculum are taught, offering a broad and balanced curriculum. Rich, memorable learning experiences including trips, visitors, workshops and practical hands-on activities are essential to bringing the curriculum to life and embedding the knowledge acquired into children's long-term memories. The use of technology is a key part of the curriculum in Y5/6 with children using chromebooks as a core tool, and working on collaborative projects with children in schools across the world through the use of Google meets and apps - making them true global citizens!
Each area of the curriculum has an Intent, Implementation and Impact document. Each curriculum area is based on a published scheme which we feel offers a knowledge rich curriculum with opportunities to develop key subject specific skills. It is used and adapted to meet the needs and interests of our children, and includes additional learning and enrichment opportunities. Each scheme organises the learning to build on prior learning and has carefully sequenced the acquisition of knowledge and development of skills. Sometimes the school has had to adapt these to fit our two-year learning cycle. The details of this and the vocabulary taught are in the scheme documents.
Each phase has a curriculum map showing the full coverage of the curriculum. Subjects are taught separately, but links are made where appropriate. Teachers use these documents as the basis for their planning, to ensure the curriculum meets the needs of each individual child.
The headteacher and deputy headteacher monitor and evaluate the planning, teaching and impact of the curriculum through regular monitoring activities which include learning walks, planning and work scrutinies, pupil conferencing and data outcomes.
Teachers work together to look at progression and outcomes through regular book looks in different subject areas across the school.
Our governing body monitors and evaluates the way the school curriculum is implemented through the use of the School Improvement Plan and the head teacher’s termly reports as well as meetings with subject leaders and /or teachers and children. End of year data outcomes in reading, writing and maths are also evaluated.
If you have any further questions about our curriculum, please talk to the headteacher, or visit our school to see it in action.

Pets As Therapy
Pets As Therapy is a charity which enables schools to have dogs visit to listen to children read. The school has seen incredible impact from this work with some of our children. If you would like to find out more about this valuable work, or make a donation to this charity, visit their website: https://petsastherapy.org/
Wider School Community
Pets As Therapy

Pupil Leaders
Our Year 6 pupils take on a variety of leadership roles during the year. They have to apply for these roles in Year 5 and are then interviewed by the previous Head Pupils and a member of the governing body. They are then offered one of the roles. They always carry out their responsibilities with pride.
The Leadership Roles
We have a very active School Council. The members of the School Council are elected by the pupils within the school. There are two representatives from Years 1-6.
Members of the School Council are elected on an annual basis. Officers are elected by the School Council members. The School Council will meet at least every two weeks. Mrs Letchford will be present at School Council meetings. Others may attend by invitation of the School Council.
Junior Road Safety Officers
Our Junior Road Safety Officers are trained by the road safety officers in Hampshire. They promote road safety to all our children through assemblies, competitions and a noticeboard.
